findings.description: Proof step 1.2 was written as five Markdown blocks separated by blank lines, so the app's step parser (paragraphs() in web/lib/item-sections.ts, consumed by ItemBody.tsx and library-pack-html.ts) matched /^(\d+\.\d+)\s+/ on only the first block: the two displays and the two continuing prose runs fell through to the unnumbered branch and the trailing tag printed as the literal text "[L5, L6, construct]" instead of chips, while steps 2.1 and 3.1 cite "step 1.2". Joined the five blocks into the one paragraph the parser expects by replacing the four blank lines with single spaces. No word, symbol, display, citation, step number or dependency changed. Verified through the app's own remark/rehype pipeline (remark-gfm + remark-math + rehype-katex, from web/node_modules): the math node sequence is identical before and after (10 inlineMath nodes, same values), the KaTeX HTML carries no katex-error, the rendered text is byte-identical, the paragraph count drops 5 -> 1, and the step now parses as number "1.2" with chips L5, L6, construct. This joined shape is the corpus norm (271 numbered steps already carry an inline $$ display). Gates after the edit: precheck 4924 checked / 0 failing, depcheck, fwdcheck, extcheck, rendercheck, prosecheck, depsource all exit 0; proof-contract --strict unchanged for this item (step 1.2 keeps its number, so the batch-9 input map still resolves).

Closed at stage step10-contract-repair by the lead Alpha, which owns research/*.proof-contracts.json; Tau's own pass left the file byte-identical because the repair could not be completed inside Tau's file scope. Sigma's diagnosis and one-line repair were both correct and were applied as written: step 1.4's three Markdown blocks were joined into one paragraph by replacing the two blank lines with single spaces, so the step parser (paragraphs() in web/lib/item-sections.ts) again matches /^(\d+\.\d+)\s+/ on the whole step. Not one word, symbol, display, citation or dependency changed. Tau had already verified this join through the app's own remark-gfm + remark-math + rehype-katex pipeline: identical math nodes (9 inlineMath, e[e^{-1}[S]]=g^{-1}[f[S]]=S\cap e[E] with its brackets intact), no katex-error, byte-identical rendered text, 3 paragraphs -> 1, and both the step number "1.4" and the chips "step 1.3, L3, algebra" parsing. The blocker Tau identified was real and was discharged in the same act. The split form had been hiding step 1.4's citation of step 1.3 from tools/precheck.mts; joined, precheck fails and prints the canonical stratification 1.4->2.1, 2.1->3.1, 3.1->4.1. That stratification was adopted, and it is honest: only step 1.4 cites a phase-1 step, so it alone moves to phase 2, and its two consumers shift behind it. Every reference moved with the step -- old 2.1's prose "using step 1.4" and tag [step 1.4, construct] became "using step 2.1" and [step 2.1, construct]; old 3.1's tag [.., step 2.1, L4] became [.., step 3.1, L4]; and its prose "steps 1.1, 1.2, and 2.1 give the left adjoint, conservativity, and preservation hypotheses" became "steps 1.1, 1.2, and 3.1", which precheck's own auto-repair does not rewrite and which would otherwise have named the pullback step where the preservation step was meant. precheck is clean on the item. The step-keyed proof contract was renumbered in the same act in research/frontier-17-batch-9.proof-contracts.json -- L3's uses 1.4->2.1 and L4's 3.1->4.1, the three moved derivation rows re-keyed with their inputs and their claim text refreshed from disk (step-2-1's claim had been truncated at "Hence [L3] gives" by the same fragmentation), and the empty and degenerate boundary evidence re-pointed from step 2.1 to step 3.1 -- then re-merged into research/frontier-17-proof-contracts.json. proof-contract --strict went from 11 errors to 0. No mathematical content was added, removed, narrowed or weakened; the item's text changed only in the two joined line breaks and the step numbering, so its item_sha256 moved and it needs a paired rejudge.

Fact [F1]'s wikilink target title is "The power series for log(1+x) on (-1,1], including the Abel endpoint"; resolveWikilinks (web/lib/math-library.ts) expands [[id]] to [<title>](/library/item/<id>), and the bare ] in "(-1,1]" closed the link label early, so the reader saw raw Markdown. Gave the link an explicit bracket-free label using the aliased form SCHEMA.md section 4 already specifies: [[thm-log-one-plus-x-power-series|The power series for log(1+x), including the Abel endpoint]]. Reproduced the defect and the fix through the real expansion regex plus the app's Markdown pipeline: before, zero <a> elements and the literal text "([The power series ... ](/library/item/...))" reaches the reader; after, exactly one <a href="/library/item/thm-log-one-plus-x-power-series"> with that label and no raw markup. The target id, the deps entry and [F1]'s own statement of the domain ("For $-1<x\le1$") are untouched, and tools/facts-block.mjs still extracts the same single id from the fact line, so depcheck/depsource/proof-contract see no change. Only the displayed label changed.

summary: All three of Sigma's findings are now repaired in place: two by Tau, and S-002 by the lead Alpha at stage step10-contract-repair, which owns the proof contracts Tau could not touch. S-001 and S-003 are closed: the fragmented proof step on prop-a-monadic-category-over-a-cocomplete-base-is-cocomplete-iff-it-has-coequalizers now parses as one numbered step with its L5/L6/construct chips, and Fact [F1] of lem-stirling-formula-up-to-a-positive-constant now renders as a working link instead of raw Markdown. Both were verified against the app's own renderer rather than by inspection -- remark-gfm + remark-math + rehype-katex out of web/node_modules for the step join (identical math nodes, no katex-error, byte-identical rendered text, paragraph count 5 -> 1, step number and chips parsing) and the real resolveWikilinks regex for the link (zero <a> before, one correct <a> after). No mathematical content was changed, removed or weakened in either: the joins replace blank lines with spaces and nothing else, and the wikilink change touches only the displayed label. S-002 is blocked and its file is byte-identical to the Tau baseline. Sigma is right about the defect and right about the one-line repair, but the same fragmentation was also hiding step 1.4's citation of step 1.3 from precheck: the split form passes, the joined form fails precheck (exit 1) demanding the canonical stratification 1.4->2.1, 2.1->3.1, 3.1->4.1, and adopting that renumbering desynchronises the item's step-keyed proof contract -- measured at 10 additional proof-contract --strict errors repairable only in research/frontier-17-batch-9.proof-contracts.json and the merged contract, neither of which Sigma named. Join, renumber and contract edit have to land together, under a role that owns research/*.proof-contracts.json. Gate state after the two repairs: precheck 4924 checked / 0 failing, depcheck, fwdcheck, extcheck, rendercheck, prosecheck, depsource, citation-fidelity, boundary-audit and finite-smoke all clean. Reported and not touched, because it is outside both Sigma's findings and Tau's authority: proof-contract --strict carries one error that predates this dispatch -- citation-quote-mismatch on thm-galois-group-of-an-irreducible-quartic-by-its-resolvent, whose L1 quote still reads "$|H\cap V_4|$" while lem-transitive-subgroups-of-s-four-and-the-resolvent-action's Statement reads "$\lvert H\cap V_4\rvert$" after the previous Tau run's table repair. It is exactly one differing line, and it is the same class of contract desync that blocks S-002. RECONCILED at stage step10-contract-repair: S-002 is closed. The join Sigma specified was applied verbatim, the canonical stratification precheck prints (1.4->2.1, 2.1->3.1, 3.1->4.1) was adopted with every prose and tag reference moved with it, and research/frontier-17-batch-9.proof-contracts.json was renumbered and re-merged in the same act. The pre-existing citation-quote-mismatch on thm-galois-group-of-an-irreducible-quartic-by-its-resolvent, reported here and correctly left untouched by Tau, was also repaired at that stage by updating the recorded L1 quote in research/frontier-17-batch-3.proof-contracts.json to the lemma's current \lvert...\rvert spelling; the consuming item's own [L1] fact line does not carry the table row, so no citation-fidelity repair was needed on the item, and the lemma was not changed back. proof-contract --strict is now 0 errors over 384 items, and precheck, depcheck, rendercheck and citation-fidelity are clean. items/thm-the-contravariant-power-set-functor-is-monadic.md requires a paired rejudge.
